<STRUCT_0001>
A <TEXTITOPEN_0001>topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0001> is the category of sheaves of sets on a site, see
Sites, Definition <REF_0001>. Hence it is customary
to refer to the use the phrase ``<ACCENT_0001>tale topos of a scheme'' to refer to
the category of sheaves on the small <ACCENT_0002>tale site of a scheme.
Here is the formal definition.

Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> The <TEXTITOPEN_0001><ACCENT_0001>tale topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0001>, or the <TEXTITOPEN_0002>small <ACCENT_0002>tale topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>
of <MATH_0002> is the category <MATH_0003> of sheaves of sets on
the small <ACCENT_0003>tale site of <MATH_0004>.
<STRUCT_0003> The <TEXTITOPEN_0003>Zariski topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0003>, or the <TEXTITOPEN_0004>small Zariski topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0004>
of <MATH_0005> is the category <MATH_0006> of sheaves of sets on the
small Zariski site of <MATH_0007>.
<STRUCT_0004> For <MATH_0008> a
<TEXTITOPEN_0005>big <MATH_0009>-topos<TEXTITCLOSE_0005> is the category of sheaves of set on a
big <MATH_0010>-topos of <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0005>

<STRUCT_0001>
Note that the small Zariski topos of <MATH_0001> is simply the category of sheaves
of sets on the underlying topological space of <MATH_0002>, see
Topologies, Lemma <REF_0001>.
Whereas the small <ACCENT_0001>tale topos does not depend on the choices made in the
construction of the small <ACCENT_0002>tale site, in general the big topoi do depend
on those choices.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
It turns out that the big or small <ACCENT_0003>tale topos only depends on the
full subcategory of <MATH_0003> or <MATH_0004> consisting of
affines, see
Topologies, Lemmas <REF_0002> and
<REF_0003>.
We will use this for example in the proof of the following lemma.
